_source: Five Parsecs: Tactics rulebook. Operational System pp.92-99; army organization p.134; Campaign Points pp.106-107.

platoon.label: Platoon
platoon.support_rule: Must have fewer supports than troops

unit_upgrade.description: Acquire a veteran skill for one unit

roster_change.description: Add or replace a unit in the roster

operational_turn_steps.name: Play all Intended Tabletop Battles
operational_turn_steps.description: Each player-controlled force is assigned to an Operational Zone; track which battles were fought in which Zone. The book sets no cap: 'any number of tabletop battles', one per operational turn by default.

operational_turn_steps.name: Apply Player Battle Points
operational_turn_steps.description: Award 1 PBP per tabletop victory in an Operational Zone; 0 for a draw or inconclusive battle. Points earned by both sides in the same Zone cancel 1-for-1.

operational_turn_steps.name: Resolve Battles
operational_turn_steps.description: A battle takes place in every Operational Zone, resolved with the Operational Combat system. Where several battles occur in one Zone, apply each result before resolving the next.

operational_turn_steps.name: Carry out Operational Orders
operational_turn_steps.description: Each faction rolls D6 on the Operational Orders table. Apply Army Strength and Zone changes first, then any Operational Combats. If two sides attack the same Zone, both get +1 Combat Die in the FIRST combat resolved there.

operational_turn_steps.name: Carry out Commando Raids
operational_turn_steps.description: Commit unspent PBP against the same or an adjacent region and roll 1D6 per point.

operational_turn_steps.name: Redeploy Forces
operational_turn_steps.description: Each faction may redeploy 1 point of Army Strength provided both armies are connected through a series of friendly territories, even if some are under attack.

operational_turn_steps.name: Open new Zones; Select new Focus
operational_turn_steps.description: Each faction that won an Operational Zone attacks an adjacent region. Attacker rolls the highest of two D6 for Army Strength; the defender rolls 1D6.

operational_turn_steps.name: Choose Player Commitments
operational_turn_steps.description: Assign each player army to an Operational Zone for the coming turn.

operational_turn_steps.name: Adjust Cohesion Scores
operational_turn_steps.description: Each time a region is lost, the losing faction's Cohesion drops by 1. At 0 that faction is defeated. The campaign is won when only one faction remains; if all remaining factions reach 0 together the war is inconclusive.
operational_turn_steps._note: ABSENT from the book's own 8-step summary list on p.96 but present as a section on p.99. It is the campaign end condition, so omitting it leaves a turn loop that can never finish.

starting_values._source_note: p.93: 'If in doubt, begin Cohesion at 5 for each side.' Cohesion is a pacing control, so a different starting value is a legitimate campaign choice.

mixed_army_rules.scenario_limit: Any combination that makes narrative sense

player_battle_points.scope: Zone- and army-specific; may be saved between operational turns.

outcomes_in_order.condition: Both sides rolled two or more 6s
Only one side rolled two or more 6s
One side rolled a single-die result higher than any of the opponent's dice
outcomes_in_order.outcome: One side gains the upper hand

outcomes_in_order.condition: Highest die for both sides is the same (a 5 or 6)
Highest die for both sides is the same (a 1, 2, 3 or 4)

operational_combat._resolution_note: Consult the outcome rows IN ORDER, top down, and use only the FIRST match -- the book states this explicitly. A roll can satisfy several rows.

table.name: Construct Defense
table.effect: One region in the faction's territory becomes a Defensible region. If not using the optional terrain types, increase Army Strength by +1 instead.

table.name: Continued Offensive
table.effect: The faction immediately fights again in an Operational Zone where it has equal or higher Army Strength.

table.name: New Offensive
table.effect: The faction attacks any region adjacent to its territory and fights immediately. Generate Army Strength normally for each side.

table.name: Renewed Effort
table.effect: Select an Operational Zone. Increase Army Strength by +1 and fight another battle.

table.name: Raiding
table.effect: If the enemy has a higher Army Strength in any Operational Zone, adjust it by -1.

table.name: Bolster Positions
table.effect: The weakest army increases Army Strength by +1.

operational_orders.less_eventful_variant: Optional: carry out only a single Operational Order each campaign turn, randomly selecting which faction acts.

commando_raids.target: the same or any adjacent region

redeploy.requires: both armies connected through a series of friendly territories
redeploy.ai_behaviour: The AI reinforces an army reduced to 1-2 Army Strength, drawing from the strongest army present.

cohesion._note: Cohesion is often lower than the number of territories, so a faction can lose while still holding territory and fielding armies.

army_destruction.at_zero_army_strength: The army can no longer contest the region; the Operational Zone ceases to exist and the area falls to the survivors.
army_destruction.mutual_destruction: The Operational Zone still ceases to exist and the region becomes neutral.
